learning_outcomes.text: Propose and analyze simple structures and suggest improvement solutions for them.
Acquire knowledge in the field of rigid and flexible solid mechanics.
Express and communicate ideas and solutions related to simple mechanisms and structures.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the study of elasticity
Analysis of deformations and stresses in elastic solids
Relationships between stresses and deformations. Elastic behavior.
Other types of material behavior
Tension-compression, bending, torsion, and shear
Introduction to the study of Elasticity: Object of Elasticity
Introduction to the study of Elasticity: Concept of solid (Types, Characteristics)
Introduction to the study of Elasticity: Static and elastic equilibrium (Section method, Efforts (types))
Introduction to the study of Elasticity: Concept of stress (Definition, Elastic equilibrium)
Stress state in elastic solids: Stress vector. Intrinsic components
Stress state in elastic solids: Stress vector at a point (Stress matrix, Stress vector in any direction)
Stress state in elastic solids: Equilibrium equation (Internal equilibrium, Boundary equilibrium)
Stress state in elastic solids: Principal stresses and directions (Characteristic equation, Invariants)
Stress state in elastic solids: Mohr's Circles (Construction, Information derived, Particular cases)
Analysis of deformations: Effects in the vicinity of a point (Translation, rotation, and dilation (without demonstration))
Analysis of deformations: Deformation matrix (Matrix, Meaning of its components, Principal directions. Characteristic equation)
Analysis of deformations: Unit strain vector in any direction (Obtaining the unit strain vector, Intrinsic components, Duality of stress vector and strain vector)
Analysis of deformations: Mohr's Circles (Generation of circles, Information, Particular cases)
Relationships between the stress matrix and the strain matrix: Stress-strain diagram (Types of behavior, Tensile test, Hooke's Law. Longitudinal modulus of elasticity E)
Relationships between the stress matrix and the strain matrix: Transverse deformations (Poisson's coefficient)
Relationships between the stress matrix and the strain matrix: Principle of superposition (Statement, Consequences)
Relationships between the stress matrix and the strain matrix: Generalized Hooke's Laws (Statement, Transverse modulus of elasticity G, Relationship E, G)
Relationships between the stress matrix and the strain matrix: Lamé's equations
Introduction to Strength of Materials: Object of Strength of Materials (Strength, stiffness, and stability, Differences between Elasticity Theory and Strength of Materials)
Introduction to Strength of Materials: Mechanical prism model (Elastic solid (recall), Characteristics (recall): center of gravity, area, moments of inertia, static moments)
Introduction to Strength of Materials: Elastic equilibrium (Solicitations, Relationship between stress matrix components and solicitations)
Introduction to Strength of Materials: General principles of Strength of Materials (Principle of relative stiffness, Principle of superposition, Saint-Venant's Principle)
Introduction to Strength of Materials: Actions (Types (CTE), Limit States: ULS and SLS, Combinations (CTE))
Introduction to Strength of Materials: Supports (Types)
Introduction to Strength of Materials: Safety coefficients (Load coefficient, Simultaneity coefficient)
Introduction to Strength of Materials: Isostatic and hyperstatic systems (External hyperstaticity, Compatibility equations)
Uniaxial tension and compression: Definition. Elastic equilibrium. Stresses (Efforts, Stresses. Bernoulli's hypothesis, Stress matrix, Mohr's circle)
Uniaxial tension and compression: Stress concentration (Definition, Examples. Tables)
Uniaxial tension and compression: State of deformations (Unit strain, Strain matrix, Displacements)
Uniaxial tension and compression: Hyperstatic tension-compression (Expression, Displacement calculation)
Uniaxial tension and compression: Temperature effect
Shear: Definition. Elastic equilibrium (Hypotheses, Stresses)
Shear: Joints
Torsion: Definition. Elastic equilibrium (Sign convention)
Torsion: Elementary Theory. Solid circular section (Hypotheses, Stresses, Deformations, Calculation)
Torsion: Calculation of efforts and deformations
Torsion: Hyperstatic torsion
Bending. Stress state: Relationships between load, shear, and bending moment (Equilibrium of the slice, Solicitation diagrams)
Bending. Stress state: Definition. Elastic equilibrium (Types of bending, Sign convention)
Bending. Stress state: Normal stresses in pure and simple bending (Hypotheses, Navier's Law, Neutral fiber. Neutral axis)
Bending. Stress state: Stresses due to shear force (Collignon-Jourawski equation)
Analysis of deformations in bending: Principle of Virtual Work for displacement calculation
assessment_rules: The final grade in continuous assessment depends on Partial Tests (35%) and the Final Exam (65%). The two partial tests cover topics 1 and 2, while the final exam covers topics 3, 4, and 5. A minimum of 5 points out of 10 combined from partial tests and the final exam is required to pass the subject. Partial test grades are not recoverable in the ordinary final exam but are recoverable in the recovery exam. The recovery exam is a single exam covering all 5 topics, with a weight of 100% on the final grade, and a minimum of 5 points out of 10 is required to pass it.
